jobs.title: Open Rank (Assistant/Associate/ Full Professor)
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: School of Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership
jobs.description:
Assistant/Associate/Full Professor
The School of Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership (SCETL) at Arizona State University invites applications for one position on the tenure track at the rank of assistant, associate, or full professor whose primary teaching and research expertise is within the field of American constitutionalism, constitutional thought, or constitutional history. The position has an anticipated start date in August 2027. Candidates should be able to teach, in addition to relevant upper-division courses in American constitutionalism, American constitutional history, or American civic thought, SCETL’s signature course “Great Debates in American Constitutionalism and Politics.” This course heavily focuses on the American Founding and American constitutional institutions (e.g. federalism, the separation of powers) and we are proud to fulfill the Arizona Board of Regents requirement for a course in American Institutions to help understand and appreciate American constitutional principles. We would particularly welcome candidates who could supplement current department strengths by teaching courses on the American Founding, the First Amendment, the Second Amendment, Montesquieu, Religion and the American Civic Tradition, American Civil-Military Relations, or the American Way or War (American military history).
About The School of Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership
U.S. News and World Report has repeatedly ranked Arizona State University (ASU) as the most innovative university in the country ahead of Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute for Technology. Contributing to that no. 1 ranking is the School of Civic & Economic Thought and Leadership, which aims to create a new kind of leader by blending tradition and innovation, and blending liberal arts and civic education. SCETL plays a leading role in the intellectual and civic life of ASU and the various communities that it serves. Because the academic mission of the School is to renew the nexus of classical liberal arts education and American civic education in a leading public university, the School’s courses aim to prepare thoughtful citizens and civic leaders for America’s constitutional republic, in civil society or public affairs, regarding domestic and international realities. The School of Civic & Economic Thought and Leadership (SCETL), entering its ninth year, is a growing academic and civic enterprise with two undergraduate majors and a minor, undergraduate certificates in Philosophy, Politics, and Economics (PPE) and Great Books in Political Thought, and two M.A. degrees in Classical Liberal Education & Civic Leadership and War & Strategy. The M.A. in War & Strategy launched in 2026 to serve the Department of Defense's Strategic Thinkers Program, a premier graduate-level initiative that prepares select mid-career officers and civilians for senior leadership in national security and defense strategy. The School also hosts an ambitious speakers program – the Civic Discourse Project – and two Centers for research and public outreach. The Center for American Civics focuses on civic education, especially American political and constitutional thought, for a broad public and for higher education and particularly for K-12 schools. The Center for the Study of Economic Liberty pursues national and international research on economic thought, debates about markets, and policies affecting economic liberty. Additionally, the School supports the Mercy Otis Warren Initiative for Women in Civic Life and Thought, an initiative that seeks to draw attention to and support female thinkers who value and work within the expansive canon of Western social and political thought. See https://scetl.asu.edu/ for more information about the School.
About The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of Arizona State University, committed to improving communities on a local, national, and global scale. We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large, curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.
About Arizona State University
ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural, and overall health of the communities it serves.

jobs.title: Associate Librarian or Librarian - Associate Dean, Research and Learning Services
jobs.institution: University of Washington: University Libraries
jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW
The Libraries at the University of Washington invites applications for the Associate Dean, Research and Learning Services at the rank of Associate Librarian or Librarian, with an anticipated start date in the first quarter of 2027. UW librarians have an annual service period of 12 months (July 1-June 30). We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in library service in a diverse and inclusive academic community.
The base salary range for this position will be $10,700- $12,500 (at the rank of Associate Librarian) and $12,500-13,250 (at the rank of Librarian) per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. An administrative supplement in the amount of $1,500 - $3,500/month will be established at time of appointment. Other compensation associated with this position may include a relocation incentive and/or a moving allowance.
UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON AND THE UW LIBRARIES
The University of Washington comprises campuses in Seattle, Bothell and Tacoma, as well as a world-class medical center. Serving all three UW campuses, the UW Libraries is an integral partner in the education, research, clinical care, and service mission of the University. Beyond the strength of its extensive collections and digital resources, the Libraries is recognized for its excellent programs and services, innovative learning and research spaces, faculty partnerships, global reach, assessment efforts and diverse award-winning staff.
RESEARCH AND LEARNING SERVICES
Research and Learning Services (RLS) provides user-centered services to the UW community through support for research, teaching, and learning. Composed of eight departments (Access Services; Assessment; Communications; Facilities; Data Services, Sciences, & Health Sciences; Open Scholarship & Publishing and Arts & Humanities; Learning Services & Social Sciences; and the Tateuchi East Asia Library), the portfolio provides public services to advance the mission of the University and the Libraries strategic goals. Units work collaboratively to build integrated services and spaces across multiple Seattle Campus Libraries.
POSITION DESCRIPTION
Reporting to the Dean of University Libraries, the Associate Dean for Research & Learning Services (RLS) provides visionary, strategic, and operational leadership for a large and dynamic portfolio of approximately 130+ staff across eight departments. The Associate Dean, RLS reports to the Dean of Libraries and is a member of the Libraries senior management team.
This position is not tenure eligible. Note: Non-represented librarians are covered under the Administrative Librarian Personnel Code currently under revision.
This position is eligible for hybrid work (on campus and remote).
SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES
Strategic Leadership and Vision
Advance and shape a shared strategic vision for Research & Learning Services, building on ongoing efforts to reimagine services in support of strategic priorities of UW Libraries and in alignment with the University of Washington's commitments to research excellence, student success, digital transformation, and public impact.
Anticipate and respond to trends in higher education, including AI-enabled research, open science, evolving scholarly communication models, and new modes of teaching and learning.
Lead, mentor, and develop a diverse workforce; build leadership capacity at all levels; and cultivate a culture of trust, accountability, and continuous learning.
Engage with campus stakeholders to advance the work of the Libraries around research, teaching and learning support.
As a member of the University Libraries' senior leadership team, participate in strategic planning, development of new initiatives, financial planning, resource and policy development, and governance.
Management
Support organizational agility, effective change management, and cross-unit collaboration.
Foster staff excellence through professional development, succession planning, and inclusive leadership practices.
Promote a robust culture of assessment and evidence-based decision-making.
Build strong partnerships with faculty, students, academic leadership, and administrative units across UW (including UW Tacoma and UW Bothell, as appropriate).
Facilitate collaboration with campus partners on digital initiatives, research infrastructure, teaching innovation, and student success programs.
Represent the Libraries on institution-wide committees and strategic initiatives.
Co-chair the Seattle Operations Group to identify, recommend, plan, coordinate, and implement pathways to align operations with the Libraries Strategic Plan, while also balancing needs of services and collections for tri-campus Libraries staff, UW students and faculty, and the broader community locally and beyond.
Work with UW Bothell and UW Tacoma to support the One Library: Three Campuses operating principles.
Collaborate with Libraries Advancement to identify funding opportunities and cultivate donor support for strategic priorities.
Ensure sustainable use of financial and human resources aligned with long-term goals.
Professional Development and Service
Contribute to the national and international research library community through leadership roles, presentations, publications, and collaboration.
Maintain awareness of emerging trends and best practices in research libraries and related fields.
Service to University Libraries, the University and the profession.
Other Duties
May act on behalf of the Dean as needed.
RANK
Position will be at the rank of Associate Librarian, or Librarian, depending on qualifications and background. See the Rank, Status, Initial Appointments, Renewal of Appointments and Promotions of UW Libraries Librarians in the Librarian Personnel Code for librarian rank appointment criteria. Note: Non-represented librarians are covered under the Administrative Librarian Personnel Code currently under revision.
BENEFITS
Librarians are academic personnel and participate in the UW Retirement Plan (UWRP) or the state’s Public Employee Retirement System (PERS) Plan 3. This is a full-time, 12-month appointment. Vacation is accrued at the rate of 26 working days per year; sick leave at the rate of 12 working days per year. No state or local income tax. A summary of benefits associated with this title/rank can be found on our Benefits page. Appointees solely employed and paid directly by a non-UW entity are not UW employees and are not eligible for UW or Washington State employee benefits.
ANTICIPATED START DATE
While we hope to fill the position in Winter quarter (Jan.-March) 2027, we are happy to work with the successful candidate to explore opportunities for an earlier or later start date.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Oklahoma Biological Survey and Biological Sciences- Vector Biology and One Health (Tenure-Track)
jobs.institution: University of Oklahoma Norman Campus: Oklahoma Biological Survey
jobs.description:
The Oklahoma Biological Survey (OBS) and the School of Biological Sciences (SBS) at the University of Oklahoma (OU) invite applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Vector Biology and One Health science with a starting date of August 16, 2027, teaching 1 course per academic year.
We seek an innovative, collaborative, and forward-looking colleague with a record of research in vector biology, whose research addresses the biological foundations of One Health and the effects of environmental change on arthropods of medical/veterinary importance and/or vector-borne diseases; who will establish a nationally recognized, student-engaged, interdisciplinary, and externally funded research program; and who will build collaborations across the University and with public, agricultural, wildlife, and health partners, and contribute to the University’s efforts to understand and respond to emerging health challenges associated with environmental and land-use as part of OU’s Lead On Strategic Plan.
Areas of interest for the ideal candidate include, but are not limited to the following: vector biodiversity and population and range dynamics, vector-host-pathogen interactions, medical and veterinary entomology, and disease ecology. We are especially interested in candidates who integrate field-based investigation with molecular, genomic, geospatial, quantitative, or predictive approaches to address questions related to vectors and vector-borne disease in the context of One Health.
The successful candidate will be expected to: (1) develop and sustain an extramurally-funded research program; (2) contribute to statewide biodiversity monitoring and environmental health surveillance through the Oklahoma Biological Survey; (3) foster interdisciplinary collaborations across OU and with governmental, tribal, agricultural, wildlife, and public-health partners; (4) mentor undergraduate and graduate students in research and experiential learning; and (5) contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in areas such as vector biology, vector–host–pathogen interactions, parasitology, medical and veterinary entomology and/or microbiology, microbial genetics, and One Health science.
The OBS is both a state agency and a research unit in the Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences affiliated with the School of Biological Sciences at OU, and is home to the Robert Bebb Herbarium, the Oklahoma Natural Heritage Inventory, and the Oklahoma Natural Areas Registry program. The SBS was recently established through the integration of the departments of Biology and Microbiology and Plant Biology to align graduate programs and research with faculty strengths and OU’s Lead On Strategic Plan.
OU invests in its faculty by providing support and resources through the Center for Faculty Excellence and Vice President for Research and Partnerships Office. The Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences supports faculty development through senior faculty mentoring, new faculty orientation series, and access to research and educational support. We encourage candidates to apply who seek to contribute to collegial and interdisciplinary research environments.

jobs.title: Visiting Assistant Professor in Writing: Technology Writing
jobs.institution: New York University: Gallatin School of Individualized Study
jobs.description:
The Gallatin School of Individualized Study at New York University (NYU) invites applications for a Visiting Assistant Professorship in technology writing to commence on September 1, 2027 and conclude on August 31, 2029.
We seek applications from writers who engage contemporary technology for a general readership. We are open to a wide range of writing practices: journalists and reporters, cultural critics, as well as creative writers who center technology as subject matter and/or through their writing process. Regardless of their area of focus, successful applicants will have a substantive body of published, general-readership work that introduces popular audiences to complex STEM concepts. The ideal candidate will write not only to reflect technological developments but will use writing to work through such developments’ ethical, philosophical, aesthetic, and political implications--including, for example, the colonial, racialized, and gendered implications of technological developments (including but not limited to generative AI).
The Visiting Assistant Professor in Writing will develop and teach four distinct courses across the Gallatin Writing Program’s curricular areas: a First-Year Writing Seminar in fall, a First-Year Research Seminar in spring, and one Advanced Writing Course each semester. The first-year courses introduce academic writing as a way of exploring and understanding ideas and emphasize writing as a process. Advanced Writing Courses are elective courses that center student writing. Across the curriculum, coursework balances thematic content with the writing and research practices relevant to the course’s disciplinary frameworks. Workshops that lead students through the writing and revision process complement seminar-style discussion of course readings. Candidates must have the ability to accommodate students of varying learning styles and skill levels within one class. They should have a considered pedagogical approach to AI.
The position is a two-year, non-renewable position, during which time the Visiting Assistant Professor will participate fully in the life of the school, through faculty meetings and special programming. A strong track record of innovative teaching across disciplines is required. Candidates are advised that all teaching at Gallatin is done on campus in New York City.
Founded in 1972, Gallatin is a liberal arts college of 1,600 undergraduate students and 160 graduate students located within the major research University of NYU. Its innovative B.A. and M.A. programs in individualized study encourage students to develop an integrated, interdisciplinary program of study that combines courses taken in the various schools of NYU with independent studies, internships, and Gallatin’s own interdisciplinary seminars, writing courses, and arts workshops. The School emphasizes excellent teaching, top level faculty research, intensive student advising and mentoring, and a unique combination of program flexibility and academic rigor. For more information about the Gallatin School, visit our website at https://gallatin.nyu.edu.
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $75,000 to $95,000.
Review of applications will begin on October 21, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled.
For questions, please contact Gallatin’s Office of Human Resources at gallatin.hr@nyu.edu, or the chair of the search committee, Ben Ratliff, at bpr212@nyu.edu.

jobs.title: Forensic Science Associate/Full Professor

jobs.description:

The area of specialization is open. Preference will be given to candidates whose expertise is not currently represented or is underrepresented among SIF faculty, or whose work contributes to a growth area such as humanitarian forensics, wildlife forensics, or forensic pathology. We are particularly interested in candidates whose research incorporates artificial intelligence, machine learning, or data visualization in ways that help bridge forensic science and digital forensics, although such expertise is preferred rather than required.
About the School:
SIF bridges science, law, and justice, offering a unique approach to forensic research and education. The School has strengths in the psychological sciences (including social, clinical, and developmental psychology, as well as psychology and law), the natural sciences (including anthropology, biology, chemistry, entomology, and genetics), and information technology (including cybersecurity and digital forensics). About the New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences:
At ASU’s New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences, we take pride in breaking down disciplinary barriers, cultivating an environment where innovative research flourishes. Our faculty are not just educators; they are trailblazers in their fields, consistently expanding the frontiers of knowledge. We invite you to join this dynamic community, where you will lead and engage in pioneering projects that redefine academic excellence.
Our interdisciplinary approach offers you unparalleled opportunities for personal and professional growth. About Arizona State University:
Arizona State University, ranked the No. 1 “Most Innovative School” in the nation by U.S. News & World Report for twelve years in succession, has forged the model for a New American University. Year after year, ASU ranks at or near the top of the list in areas that matter. ASU is a comprehensive public research institution, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves. ASU operates on the principles that learning is a personal and original journey for each student; that they thrive on experience and that the process of discovery cannot be bound by traditional academic disciplines. Through innovation and a commitment to accessibility, ASU has drawn pioneering researchers to its faculty even as it expands opportunities for qualified students, attracting some of the highest- quality students from all 50 states and more than 130 nations. The Laboratory for Laser Energetics (LLE) is seeking candidates for the position of Assistant Scientist in the Omega Experiments Group to lead experiments in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) and related physics on OMEGA, OMEGA EP, NIF, and future laser facilities. Laser Direct Drive (LDD) implosions of DT cryogenic targets and focused physics experiments to establish a foundation for the pursuit of high-yield LDD using future broad bandwidth laser drivers, as well as nuclear, hydrodynamic, high-energy-density (HED) and magnetized plasma physics, are among the Omega Experiments Group’s key missions within the science-based Stockpile Stewardship Program (SSP) of the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). The successful candidate will perform research and development for the Omega Laser Facility and future, planned experimental facilities (e.g., the OMEGA-Next facility for ICF with broad bandwidth laser drivers, the Next-Generation HED facility). The research scope of this position encompasses the research, development, and use of x-ray and/or nuclear diagnostics to understand the behavior of extreme states of matter created on Omega for the ICF and HEDP research fields and to plan target physics experiments for future laser facilities under development at LLE. The position requires a candidate with expertise in x-ray and/or nuclear diagnostics who can lead technical, engineering, and scientific staff in the development, deployment, and use of novel ICF and HEDP diagnostics on Omega, and work with theoretical and computational experts to design target physics experiments and interpret the experimental results. The successful candidate will interact routinely with subject matter experts worldwide in ICF and HEDP research communities.
Essential Job Responsibilities
Lead ICF and related physics campaigns on the Omega Laser Facility and/or NIF
Develop advanced measurement techniques to diagnose ICF implosions and related experimental platforms using state-of-the-art x-ray or nuclear diagnostics
Collaborate with theoretical and computational experts to design ICF and HEDP target physics experiments and to achieve a physical understanding of experimental results
Collaborate with the world’s leading experts in HEDP and ICF research fields on the Omega Laser Facility and NIF by defining x-ray and nuclear diagnostic configurations, collecting experimental data, and interpreting the experimental results
Perform research and development for the future, planned experimental facilities at LLE (e.g., OMEGA-Next facility) and the NNSA complex

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researchers,  Baslan Lab
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: School of Veterinary Medicine Postdoctoral
jobs.description:
Faculty Mentor: Timour Baslan, Ph.D.
Department: Biomedical Sciences
Positions are funded by various grants: federal as well as foundation.
Five positions
The positions are open to US citizens and foreign nationals.
The Baslan Lab at the Department of Biomedical Sciences, the University of Pennsylvania (Penn) is recruiting Postdoctoral Fellows (computational & experimental), 5 positions in total, to join our multidisciplinary team of investigators. Our work focuses on studying cancer genomes, with a specific attention to the genetics and biology of a cryptic class of cancer associated mutations termed Copy Number Alterations (CNAs). These somatic events change the number and composition of chromosomes in cancer cells to yield cancer and immune biology that is almost entirely unknown.
To dissect these events, we employ a systems biology, top-down approach where advanced analytics of large datasets are coupled to focused perturbations (ex: shRNA, CRISPR, cDNA screens) in experimental model systems (e.g. organoid & cell line models). We also apply a bottom-up approach where we employ cutting edge methods to dissect novel model systems we develop (ex: mouse models).
Some of the techniques our group develops and applies are:
- advanced sequencing technologies, at single cell and bulk levels, to generate large multi-modal datasets.
- novel algorithms & computational approaches, based on maths, statistics, & machine learning, to nominate novel cancer therapeutic targets.
- innovative, molecularly engineered model systems in in-vitro and in-vivo settings (e.g. mouse models)
- highly parallel perturbation approaches; CRISPR, shRNA, PROTACs, small molecules
We aim to advance:
- novel therapeutics; targeted as well as immunotherapies
- early diagnostic as well as prognostic tools
- novel technologies that can be leveraged to address outstanding biological questions
Disease areas of focus include, but are not limited to, acute leukemias, sarcomas, as well as breast and pancreatic cancers.
The training/mentorship opportunities are in the following areas (among others):
- Developing computational and chemical biology approaches to advance copy number informed precision therapies.
- Studying cancer-immune cell interactions during cancer initiation and progression using functional biology approaches &
advanced in-situ sequencing/data analytics.
- Developing machine learning approaches to advance novel prognostic and diagnostic methods in cancer.
- Dissecting cancer genome evolution using the first of their kind, somatic lineage tracing mouse models,
along with human data analysis.
- Developing single-cell as well as circulating tumor free DNA sequencing technologies.
- Designing and applying novel comparative oncogenomic algorithms to advance unifying principles of chromosomal biology in cancer.
Prospective trainees can expect the followings: Mentorship, Freedom, Resources, Exciting Science, & Fun.
Further details can be found here: http://baslanlab.com

jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science of the University of Texas at Austin is recruiting for full-time, professional track faculty (Lecturer, Assistant Professor of Instruction, Associate Professor of Instruction, Professor of Instruction) positions. We encourage applications from candidates who will join our welcoming community and contribute to it through excellence in teaching and other contributions to the academic enterprise.
The department is consistently ranked among the top computer science programs in the nation. As of Fall 2026, Computer Science is one of three academic units in UT Austin’s new School of Computing, alongside Statistics and Data Sciences and Information. The new School is designed to strengthen collaboration and create new opportunities for cross-departmental research and education. We are renowned for our collegial environment that fosters innovation and collaboration—an environment that attracts many top-notch faculty and excellent students from across Texas, the country, and the world. We value undergraduate education and have a committed group of highly effective educators, who are committed to helping all students reach the high standards, both technical and holistic, expected of our graduates. Our instructional faculty typically teach three courses a semester, with two of those courses usually being instances of the same course. Our class sizes tend to be on the smaller side of most of our peer departments: in Fall 2024, each faculty member taught an average of 230 students across three courses. The Department is responsive to the needs of dual career couples and supports work-life balance through an array of family-friendly policies. For more information about the department, please visit https://cs.utexas.edu.
Austin, the capital of Texas, is a major technology hub, home to significant operations from companies such as Amazon, AMD, Apple, Applied Materials, AT&T, Dell, Google, IBM, Meta, NVIDIA, Samsung, Silicon Labs, and Tesla. Nestled at the edge of the Texas Hill Country, much of Austin’s lifestyle is driven by outdoor activities, media, and music, due to the availability of green space, the presence of Lady Bird Lake (a consequence of a dammed river) running through town, and the location of events such as SxSW and ACL Music Festival, to name a select few. Check out our local public radio station KUT’s Field Guide to Austin for a wide variety of Austin topics or the Austin Visitor Center’s site for information on things to do.
Position Description
For this position, the primary duty is teaching undergraduate courses, which includes a wide variety of opportunities, though teaching in our in-person and online graduate programs may be possible for some candidates. While these positions are not eligible for tenure, they have opportunities for advancement, and we hire with the intent that new instructional faculty will become a lasting part of our community.
Teaching Opportunities
Teaching opportunities range from introductory computer science courses, such as data structures, discrete mathematics, and computer architecture, to advanced courses, particularly topics related to artificial intelligence, computer systems, and UI/UX. We have opportunities to teach classes dedicated to CS majors as well as classes targeted to majors from other disciplines—many of our instructional faculty teach both types of classes. Our curriculum offers students an opportunity to investigate the social impact of computer science, and so we have opportunities to develop and teach classes that are technical with social impact considerations integrated into the content as well as stand alone technical courses and those related to social impact and ethics. We expect deep expertise in each faculty member’s subject area and value a willingness to teach related topics or introductory courses as course needs change.
Additional Contributions to the Academic Enterprise
In addition to teaching, instructional faculty at UT Austin are also expected to contribute to the academic enterprise through active service, research, mentoring, or any combination of the three. Each faculty member creates their own unique set of contributions based on interest, skill sets, and need, but we do expect our instructional faculty to spend some of their time encouraging and mentoring students towards careers in industry, government, and the academy, as well as developing and improving the curriculum within their courses. Instructional faculty have the opportunity to contribute through committee service, too, as they serve on and chair committees along with other faculty in the department.

NYUAD’s J-Term courses are designed as two-week, intensive, and highly immersive learning experiences during January. They intensify student focus, reach beyond the classroom to incorporate experiential learning, and are site-specific, engaging students deeply with the people and the place where they study. Intellectually linked to their locations, the courses take advantage of local resources; explore the history, culture, economy, and society of the host communities; and often involve collaborative activities with local students and experts. The courses illuminate the interdependence of local knowledge and global awareness while fostering cross-cultural research and insights into complex global issues.
Taking a single course during J-Term gives students more time for concentrated reflection on a dedicated topic than is the case during the semester when students must split their time between several courses. The intensity of the shared experience also forges a strong bond between the students and their professors. Although the J-Term is short, it has a great impact because of its immersive character and linking of theoretical and experiential learning. All NYUAD undergraduates must complete two J-Term courses as a requirement for graduation.
One of the defining features of our J-Term courses is that each centers on a significant, hard-to-answer, timely, and timeless question that the faculty and students explore together through multiple disciplinary and cultural lenses. A second defining feature of the J-Term courses is their pedagogy. Faculty and students explore answers to their big questions through a deep dive into how that question plays out in the sociocultural context of the location in which the course is held. J-Term courses take place in Abu Dhabi, at one of the fifteen NYU Global sites, and in different cities throughout the world. The courses must create opportunities for the class to use direct experience in the local community as an additional “text” for the classroom.

This three-session course explores how entertainment teams make decisions when audience behavior, data, creative judgment, business priorities, and organizational realities do not always point in the same direction. 2. Evaluate competing creative, audience, and business priorities using data, experimentation, and strategic judgment.

jobs.institution: Hamilton College: Hamilton College Faculty
jobs.description:
The Art Department at Hamilton College invites applications for a Visiting Assistant Professor with expertise in printmaking whose work is grounded in studio practice, scholarship and teaching. The successful candidate’s research and teaching will situate the practice of printmaking within historical, cultural, and interdisciplinary frameworks. This is a temporary one-year position for the 2027-28 academic year. In addition to teaching printmaking at the introductory and advanced level, the position will require teaching one course in introductory drawing or introductory painting. Teaching expectation is three courses in the fall and two courses in the spring, with additional responsibility for mentoring senior concentrators. The successful candidate can expect active support for their creative work. We are seeking candidates who can demonstrate their experience in teaching or working with broadly diverse student populations while contributing to a vibrant learning community that values academic freedom, creativity, and intellectual curiosity. Your cover letter should address the ways in which you would enhance the educational experience of students and further the College’s educational goals.
This position requires a strong grounding in printmaking skills, including the ability to manage a printmaking studio. The successful candidate will have the ability to teach a strong foundation in perceptual, formal, conceptual and critical skills within a liberal arts context and to engage students in the social and theoretical dimensions of printmaking as a contemporary practice. We seek candidates who possess a capacity to interweave theory and practice, who demonstrate effective collaborative skills, and who display a commitment to undergraduate education in the liberal arts.
The Art department at Hamilton College is a vibrant and robust department of six fulltime faculty serving 15-20 concentrators per year, as well as hundreds of non-major students each year. We are fortunate to teach in a state-of-the-art building that was completed in 2014 and which supports both analog practices as well as emerging technologies across 2D, 3D and time-based media offerings. Additional information about our program can be found at https://academics.hamilton.edu/art/list-art-studios.
Candidates must have an MFA, a record of effective teaching in higher education, and a demonstrated record of scholarly and creative achievement. Please contact help@interfolio.com if you have questions or problems with your uploads. Questions regarding the search may be directed to Katharine Kuharic at kkuharic@hamilton.edu. Applications will begin to be considered on January 31, 2027 and the position will remain open until filled.

jobs.description:
Tenure-track Assistant Professor in AI World Models for Embodied Systems
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
College of Engineering
Position Overview
The College of Engineering at The Ohio State University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor. We seek candidates who advance the computational foundations of AI world models: models that inherently learn general representations of physical environments, predict how those environments evolve, and reason about the consequences of actions. The goal would be to exploit world models to close the gap between simulation-trained AI and dependable real-world autonomy. Relevant research would leverage multimodal and spatiotemporal learning, context-informed and knowledge (e.g., physics)-grounded AI, generative and predictive modeling, learned simulation models and digital twins, and embodied or agentic AI. Representative grand-challenge application drivers for candidates’ research would include water resource management, infrastructure inspection, swarm operations, adaptive traffic and pedestrian flow management for next-generation urban mobility, robotics, and mobility based on agentic, autonomous, cooperative, resilient, and secure AI platforms.
The position will be anchored in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering (70%), with a joint appointment (30%) determined by the candidate’s expertise and interest in one of three units with embodied systems: the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geodetic Engineering, the Knowlton School of Architecture, or the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. This position is located on the main Columbus campus of The Ohio State University and starts as early as Fall 2027.
Performance Objectives
• Lead or co-lead a research program in foundational world-model methods, including domain-grounded data generation, multimodal perception, physics-grounded predictive models, or learned simulation and digital twins.
• Collaborate across Engineering units and campus living labs.
• Mentor PhD, MS, and undergraduate students, with attention to broadening participation in embodied AI and robotics.
• Contribute to potentially blended curriculum development that enriches traditional offerings in AI and engineering at the graduate and undergraduate levels.
• Pursue external funding to sustain and grow the research program, including continued NSF, DOE, DOT, and industry support.
• Engage with campus, industry, and government stakeholders (facilities, transportation, public safety) as an integral part of the research.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
· PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field of Engineering, Physics, or Applied Mathematics, completed by the position start date.
· A strong record of research in world models and related areas such as embodied AI, robot learning, computer vision, multimodal models integrating vision, language, geometry, sensor streams, and/or engineering data, 3D/4D scene understanding, reasoning, planning, physics-grounded AI, or simulation-based learning.
· Demonstrated ability (or clear potential, for junior candidates) to secure competitive external research funding.
· Commitment to graduate and undergraduate teaching and mentorship.
Desired:
· Experience with multimodal sensing, 3D/4D representations, multi-robot systems, or aerial and ground platforms.
· Experience with physics-informed, causal, or hybrid physics-AI models.
· Background in learned simulators, differentiable simulation, digital twins, computer graphics, or physical simulation.
· Experience with uncertainty, robustness, and generalization in open, changing, or partially observed physical environments.
· Visionary Mindset: The ability to articulate a clear research agenda that addresses fundamental challenges in current AI models, such as reasoning, generalization, and robustness.
· Evidence of research excellence in mathematical and theoretical frameworks in computing.
· Leadership qualities and vision for contributing to a nationally recognized research center.
· Experience with developing new courses and degree programs.
· A commitment to interdisciplinary education and collaborative research.
· A track record of interdisciplinary collaboration.
Skills required for success
Leadership and Collaboration: The candidate should demonstrate leadership and the ability to collaborate effectively in an academic setting.
Mentoring and Teaching: Experience or training in mentoring and teaching is desirable.
Communication Skills: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills are required, with a focus on working constructively, decisively, and collegially with both external and internal colleagues and interdisciplinary teams.
Independence and Initiative: We value individuals who can work independently and are proactive self-starters with strong project leadership skills.
Innovative Thinking: The candidate should be open to sharing ideas, continuously learn, and display innovative thinking.
Additional Information
The final offer for this position will be determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Salary and start-up packages are negotiated by the department chair and may vary depending on individual circumstances.

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) (https://ece.osu.edu/) at The Ohio State University invites applications for two tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor, with one position in each of the following two areas: 1) AI algorithmic foundations and methodologies and 2) Agentic AI foundations and methodologies. All applicants are strongly encouraged to indicate their preferred area of consideration in their cover letter, even if the applicants whose expertise span both areas.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Music, Science, and Health, Natalie L. Haslam College of Music, Fall 2027
jobs.institution: The University of Tennessee - Knoxville: Natalie L. Haslam College of Music
jobs.description:
The Knoxville campus of the University of Tennessee seeks candidates who have the ability to promote an atmosphere where all members of the university community feel welcome and can thrive.
The Natalie L. Haslam College of Music invites applications for a 9-month tenure-track position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level in Music, Science, and Health. This is a rare and forward-looking appointment designed for a scholar-teacher who believes that a fuller understanding of music — how we hear it, perform it, feel it, analyze it, and create it — is enriched by understanding the human brain, human behavior, and the science behind how we interact with the art of music and human health.
The successful candidate will occupy a distinctive role at the intersection of music, medicine and health, neuroscience, psychology, cognitive science, or other theoretical and applied sciences, contributing to both the core curriculum of the College and to an emerging cross-disciplinary research culture. The candidate will work in the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music with potential for collaboration with other colleges, and relevant health organizations.The successful candidate is expected to have either existing or strong potential for obtaining extramural funding.
Teaching Responsibilities may include:
Core lab-sequence instruction in music integrated with perspectives from the natural or social sciences appropriate to the candidate's expertise
Seminars in areas such as music and health, music perception and psychoacoustics, the neuroscience of musical experience, and other topics relevant to the candidate’s field
Student mentorship and research supervision in the candidate’s core field and related interdisciplinary fields
Online course development and delivery, with interest in expanding the College's reach into digital learning environments
Research Profile
We seek a candidate with an active research agenda that intersects with one or more of the following areas:
Scientific applications of health, wellbeing, and/or and human development, including scientific approaches to understanding music’s role in health-related outcomes.
The neuroscience of musical experience, including brain-music interaction, with particular attention to musical and cognitive aspects such as rhythm, harmony, melody, tonality, memory, and emotion.
Computational, data-driven, and/or psychological approaches to music perception, emotion, musical structure, and performance, with a focus on their relationships to human health
Machine learning and artificial intelligence applications for understanding how music interacts with human health, behavior, and perception
Web Page: www.music.utk.edu
The University of Tennessee Natalie L. Haslam College of Music offers a broad and comprehensive professional music program at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. The College has approximately 65 faculty members and approximately 400 music majors.

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is the state’s flagship research institution, a campus of choice for outstanding undergraduates, and a premier graduate institution. As a land-grant university, it is committed to excellence in learning, scholarship, and engagement with society. jobs.title: The Levitt Justice Lab S2027: Constitutional Moments
jobs.institution: Hamilton Fellowships - Levitt Center: Hamilton Fellowships - Levitt Center
jobs.description:
The Levitt Center invites students to apply to this Spring ‘27 Justice Lab “Constitutional Moments: Creating, Sustaining, and Changing How We Govern with Professors Frank Anechiarico, Ty Seidule, Heather Sullivan, and Benj Widiss.
As the United States enters its second 250 years with the oldest codified constitution in the world, is it time for another constitutional moment? Trust in the federal government sits at or near historic lows, and confidence in the electoral process itself has slipped alongside it. Meanwhile, a movement most people have never heard of is quietly approaching a constitutional threshold: twenty states have already passed applications for an Article V Convention of the States. Whether or not you think the constitutional order is in crisis, more people are asking foundational questions about it than at any point in a generation; Who gets to write the rules? Who gets to change them? And what happens when the answers stop feeling legitimate to the people governed by them?
This Justice Lab will give students the tools to think rigorously about those questions – not as abstractions, but as lived, contested, and repeatedly re-imagined processes, approached through historical, legal, comparative, and aesthetic lenses. Students will step into the shoes of the original framers to write the Constitution, then reconvene as a hypothetical Convention of the States to amend it. They will analyze constitutional law through landmark court cases and the doctrines that underpin them. They will study how other countries in the Americas have handled constitutional rupture and refounding. And they will trace how the founding moment itself has never stopped being rewritten, from the founding documents as rhetorical performances through two centuries of American fiction, poetry, and film that reclaim, contest, and re-stage it. Students will leave with a working command of constitutional design, argument, and interpretation: how constitutions get made, how they break, and how they get imaginatively remade.
Experiential learning for this Justice Lab will include two long form role playing games in COLEG/GOVT/HIST281. The Constitutional Convention of 1787 focuses on the most fundamental political and legal event in American history. Students in the game, playing the actual delegates to the Convention, gather in “Philadelphia” to write a new constitution for the United States. The second game creates a hypothetical “Convention of the States” to add amendments to the Constitution. Students will also have a required evening event in mid-April.
Required Courses:
GOVT-273W / PPOL-273W: Revolution and Re-Foundings in Latin America with Heather Sullivan (M/W 1:00 - 2:15PM)
Nearly all Latin American countries gained independence in the 1800s, but unlike in the United States, many of their constitutions from this period have been swept away. Revolutions and large-scale constitutional reforms occurred throughout the 20th century and into the 21st. Some of these constitutional reforms were seen as a way to address profound socioeconomic and racial inequalities in the region. Others have been a tool for concentrating executive power. Some were motivated by both currents. This class will explore the causes and effects of these constitutional re-foundings as well as the processes through which they occurred. This is a writing-intensive course.
COLEG-281 / GOVT-281 / HIST-281: Common Ground: A Laboratory for Civil Discourse with Ty Seidule (T/Th 10:30 - 11:45 AM)
From the beginning of the American experiment, political leaders and citizens have struggled over how to create a democracy, how to sustain it, how to operate it fairly, and even how to discuss it. Discourse has always been contested – and not always civilly. The course consists primarily of two complex roleplaying games to help us understand how America created its constitution and how we might change it. The first game, The Constitutional Convention of 1787: Constructing the American Republic places students in the actual roles of the founding fathers in Philadelphia. The next game is “Convention of the States: Toward a More Perfect Union?” In this scenario, the states have exercised Article V of the US Constitution, calling all the states together “for proposing Amendments.” Can we change the Constitution? We’ll try. This is a speaking intensive course.
GOV241: Survey of Constitutional Law with Frank Anechiarico (T/Th 1:00 - 2:15PM)
In this course, students will analyze constitutional doctrines through major cases. We will examine the function of the Supreme Court as an instrument of government and arbiter of public policy as well as core doctrines including judicial review, federalism, interstate commerce, due process and questions of individual rights.
Prerequisites for this course are waived for Justice Lab participants
LIT2XX: Reconstituting the Constitution with Benjamin Widiss (M/W 2:30 - 3:45PM)
This course explores the Constitutional “Moment” as an extended sociocultural formation in the decades just before and after the turn of the nineteenth century, and as a recurring American phenomenon thereafter. We will begin by analyzing the founding documents as rhetorical performances, reading the aspirations and anxieties they express in relation to those legible in contemporaneous literary texts. Then we’ll turn to political, literary, and cinematic works across subsequent American generations that reclaim or figuratively re-stage the founding moment even as they radically re-frame its stakes and stakeholders. Likely authors: A. Hamilton, T. Jefferson, W. Irving, H.D. Thoreau, F. Douglass, E.C. Stanton, W. Whitman, A. Lincoln, G. Stein, R. Ellison, G. Lucas, L.M. Miranda.

The Casanova laboratory employs a diverse array of methodologies to discover the causes and mechanisms of severe or fatal illness in some individuals during their initial infection, contrasting with the resilience of most people to the same infection. To efficiently address this challenging question, our lab is structured into five collaborative research teams, each dedicated to investigating specific themes (three infections, a mechanism of disease, and a methodological approach).
Dr. Bertrand Boisson leads the laboratory’s pyogenic infection research program. Using innovative genome-wide approaches, his team identifies disease-causing genetic variants in children with invasive staphylococcal or pneumococcal disease and uncovers novel mechanisms underlying severe bacterial infections. They investigate the genetic predisposition to isolated congenital asplenia (ICA) and the function and disorders associated with the canonical NF-κB pathway in humans, with particular emphasis on disorders associated with its dysregulation, including autoinflammatory and autoimmune diseases. Our research is funded by HHMI, several NIH grants and the Lupus Research Alliance.
The candidate will learn genetic approaches to identify candidate variants and genes in individual patients and cohorts. They will test hypotheses of genetic homogeneity at the variant and gene levels, as well as genetic heterogeneity. They will perform short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing and transcriptomics, cellular biology, cell culture, spectral flow cytometry, and high-throughput bioinformatic analyses.
Information on our postdoctoral training program, benefits, and a virtual tour can be found at http://www.utsouthwestern.edu/postdocs.

jobs.title: Jay I. Kislak Artist-in-Residence
jobs.institution: University of Miami: Jay I. Kislak Collection
jobs.description:
The Jay I. Kislak Collection at the University of Miami Libraries houses a large collection that focuses on cultural encounters and their legacies across the Americas. These materials include rare books, manuscripts, contemporary artists’ books and zines, graphic art, maps, photographs, and broadsides. The Jay I. Kislak Artist-in-Residence program is made possible through a generous endowment provided by the Kislak Foundation to promote the collection’s use through scholarly pursuits.
Residencies of up to two months will support those who wish to use the Kislak Collection to advance their artistic practice. The artist can be at any stage of their career and in any discipline, such as literary, visual, and performing arts. The artist-in-residence will collaborate with the Kislak Collection and Special Collections to create works inspired by our collection materials. jobs.title: LEO Lecturer I, EXS 185, Winter 2027, Flint Public Health & Sciences Department, College of Health Sciences (Onsite)

jobs.description:
Be at the forefront of change and become part of the innovative and forward-thinking academic team at the University of Michigan-Flint's Public Health & Health Sciences Department in the rapidly expanding College of Health Sciences. The Exercise Science Program at UM-Flint is seeking a LEO Lecturer I for the Winter 2027 semester to teach for EXS 185 - Motor Control of Movement at 25% effort. This is an in-person course, with days and times for the course TBD.
Course Description: Examination of motor development, motor learning, and motor control as they relate to physical literacy, movement competency, and skill acquisition across the lifespan. Emphasis is placed on theoretical and physiological foundations of movement, the development of postural control and mobility, and the influence of individual, task, and environmental constraints on movement strategies. jobs.title: Adjunct Instructors of Management Communications Program (2027-2028)
jobs.institution: New York University: Management Communication Program
jobs.description:
The Management Communication Program at the Stern School of Business is accepting applications for adjunct instructors in its first-year core writing courses. This writing-intensive curriculum examines the relationship between business and society to build students’ writing and critical-thinking skills while introducing them to business inquiry.
The fall course, Commerce & Culture, focuses on representations of business in fiction—novels, films, plays, and short stories. Through discussion-based sessions and analytical papers, students examine how texts portray the interplay of market forces, society, and individuals. The spring course, Business & Society, turns to the theoretical texts underlying economic and business discourse (from Adam Smith to Elinor Ostrom to R. Edward Freeman), teaching students to engage with conceptual texts and apply them to contemporary business situations. Writing assignments include analytical claims about conceptual ideas, research-based analysis of social issues, and proposals for business action.
Adjunct Faculty at Stern are part-time instructors, hired on a term-by-term basis. Responsibilities typically include teaching one to two classes per year. Most appointments are made 6-9 months in advance. However, applications are welcome at any time and will be kept on file for future openings.
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the contact hour rate for the positions are:
Adjunct Assistant Professor: $300 - $470
Adjunct Associate Professor: $380 - $500
Adjunct Professor: $400 - $650
This rate is based on the collective bargaining agreement with Local 7902.
Applications to teach the Spring 2027 Business & Society course will receive priority if submitted by October 25, 2026. We are also accepting applications for the Fall 2027 Commerce & Culture course through January 31, 2027, and welcome candidates with the interest and capacity to teach both courses.

jobs.title: ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES: Introduction to Environmental Studies

jobs.description:

Introduction to Environmental Studies is a gateway course in the Environmental Studies Program, introducing students to a broad range of perspectives on environmental issues and their social, cultural, and ecological dimensions.
